_meta.what_this_is: The CURRENT Firebase backend, field by field, and where every field goes in Supabase.
_meta.source: parsed from lib/backend/schema/*.dart — the FlutterFlow-generated Firestore models
_meta.coverage_guarantee: Every source field is mapped, exploded into a new table, or dropped with a reason. The generator fails if any field is unaccounted for.
_meta.caveat: Parsed from the Dart models, so it shows what the APP knows about. Fields added directly in the Firebase console that FlutterFlow never modeled will not appear here — verify against a real export.

how_to_read_this.firestore_type: the type as stored in Firestore today
how_to_read_this.what_it_is: plain-English meaning of the field right now
how_to_read_this.points_to: for DocumentReference fields: which collection it references
how_to_read_this.migrates_to: the Postgres table.column it becomes, or "— DROPPED —"
how_to_read_this.transform: copy | rename | cast | FLATTEN map | EXPLODE array | RESOLVE reference | MERGE | DROP

auth.user_doc_link: users/{uid} — the Firestore doc id IS the Firebase Auth uid

becomes.email/password: DONE — enabled and tested. Email confirmation is OFF, so signup returns a session immediately, matching v1 behaviour.
becomes.google: TODO — needs a client ID + secret in the Supabase dashboard, and the native iOS/Android config to match. Use signInWithIdToken from supabase_flutter.
becomes.apple: TODO — needs a Services ID + key from the Apple Developer account.
becomes.anonymous: DROPPED (decision, 2026-09-18). Nothing in the v1 UI ever called it — verified by grep; it was FlutterFlow scaffolding. Not enabled on Supabase.

auth.hardest_part: Firebase hashes passwords with modified scrypt; Supabase uses bcrypt. Import the Firebase hash parameters, and VERIFY on throwaway accounts before choosing a cutover date. Fallback is a forced password reset for every user.
auth.import_gotcha: Imported users MUST be written with email_confirmed_at already set. Firebase treated them as verified; importing them unconfirmed would lock out the entire existing user base.

id_mapping.problem: Firestore stores relationships as DocumentReference PATHS ("users/abc123"). Postgres needs UUIDs.
id_mapping.solution: Build an id_map in pass 1 over every collection, then resolve all references in pass 2.
id_mapping.table: id_map(collection text, firestore_id text, uuid uuid, primary key (collection, firestore_id))
id_mapping.special_case_users: profiles.id MUST equal the auth.users.id created by the auth import — NOT a fresh uuid. Run the auth migration FIRST, then seed id_map for users from its output.
id_mapping.keep_after_migration: yes — it makes verification, re-runs and rollback possible

enums._today: Declared in Dart but stored in Firestore as plain strings. Nothing validates them, and several fields that should use them (lawns.status, shirt_requests.shirt_level, users.gender) are free text.

ShirtLevel.becomes: badge_levels rows (a table, not an enum — levels are admin-editable)

new_tables.children: Exploded from users.group_detail. Columns: id, profile_id FK, name, shirt_size, gender.
new_tables.badge_request_children: Exploded from shirt_requests.group_detail. Columns: id, badge_request_id FK, name, shirt_size, gender.
new_tables.lawn_photos: Exploded from lawns.photos. Columns: id, lawn_id FK, photo_kind, url, blurhash, sort_order. A child table rather than four fixed columns, because settings.max_lawn_photos is configurable and the v2 Figma flow shows different photo steps (lawnpic / action / safety).
new_tables.user_roles: Replaces the world-readable admins collection. Surfaced into the JWT so RLS can read it cheaply.
new_tables.featured_members: Holds leaderboards.star_of_month, the one thing the leaderboard view cannot derive. Columns: id, region, profile_id FK, month.
new_tables.app_settings: The scalar remainder of the settings document, single-row guarded.

deleted_collections.leaderboards: Replaced by the leaderboard SQL view. star_of_month moves to featured_members; everything else is derived.
deleted_collections.admins: Replaced by user_roles + a JWT claim. It was world-readable and client-creatable.
deleted_collections.ff_push_notifications: FlutterFlow push queue — replaced by a Postgres trigger + Edge Function.

16. run recalc_profile_totals() over every profile, then diff against the imported values
